docs.title: Lixy Documentation
docs.text: Welcome to the Lixy documentation! Lixy is a modern GitOps deployment platform designed specifically for LXC containers.

docs.title: What is Lixy?
docs.text: Lixy provides a declarative, Git-based approach to managing LXC container deployments. By storing your infrastructure configuration in Git repositories, Lixy automatically reconciles the desired state with the actual state of your deployments, ensuring consistency and enabling powerful GitOps workflows.

docs.title: 🔄 GitOps-Based Deployments
docs.text:
• Declare your infrastructure as code in Git repositories
  • Automatic reconciliation of desired vs. actual state
  • Version-controlled deployment history
  • Easy rollbacks and auditing

docs.title: 🔐 Secure Authentication
docs.text:
• Built-in user authentication with JWT tokens
  • Agent-based authentication for LXC hosts
  • Role-based access control (admin/user)
  • Secure credential management for container registries

docs.title: 📦 Container Registry Integration
docs.text:
• Seamless integration with GitHub Container Registry (GHCR)
  • Support for private registries
  • Automatic image tag resolution
  • Version strategy support (semver, stability, patterns)

docs.title: 🎯 Drift Detection & Self-Healing
docs.text:
• Automatic detection of configuration drift
  • Self-healing capabilities to restore desired state
  • Configurable drift detection intervals
  • Protected services support

docs.title: 🚀 Easy to Use
docs.text:
• Simple CLI for all operations
  • Modern web dashboard (Vue 3 + Vuetify)
  • RESTful API for automation
  • Comprehensive documentation

docs.title: 🏗️ Flexible Architecture
docs.text:
• Controller-agent architecture
  • Multi-agent support for distributed deployments
  • Template-based deployment configurations
  • Environment-specific variable management

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Go 1.21 or higher
  • LXC/LXD installed on target hosts
  • Git
  • Docker (for container images)

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/MinaroShikuchi/lixy.git
cd lixy

# Build the controller
cd cmd/lixy
go build -o lixy

# Build the agent
cd ../lixies
go build -o lixies

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
# Start the controller
./lixy

# Register an agent (on LXC host)
./lixies register --controller http://controller:8080 --token <registration-token>

# Create a deployment
lixy create deployment my-app --target agent1 --compose docker-compose.yml

# List deployments
lixy get deployments

# Reconcile from Git repository
lixy reconcile environment dev --repository lixy-cd

docs.title: Deploying Documentation to GitHub Pages
docs.text: This guide will walk you through deploying your Lixy documentation to GitHub Pages using MkDocs.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Git repository hosted on GitHub
  • Python 3.7 or higher installed
  • Write access to the repository

docs.title: Step 1: Install MkDocs and Dependencies
docs.text:
# Install MkDocs and required plugins
pip install mkdocs mkdocs-material pymdown-extensions

Verify installation: 

mkdocs --version
# Should output: mkdocs, version 1.5.x or higher

docs.title: Step 2: Create MkDocs Configuration
docs.text:
Create a file named mkdocs.yml in your project root (same level as docs/ folder):

site_name: Lixy Documentation
site_description: GitOps deployment platform for LXC containers
site_author: Your Name
site_url: https://yourusername.github.io/lixy

repo_name: yourusername/lixy
repo_url: https://github.com/yourusername/lixy
edit_uri: edit/main/docs/

theme:
  name: material
  palette:
    # Light mode
    - scheme: default
      primary: indigo
      accent: indigo
      toggle:
        icon: material/brightness-7
        name: Switch to dark mode
    # Dark mode
    - scheme: slate
      primary: indigo
      accent: indigo
      toggle:
        icon: material/brightness-4
        name: Switch to light mode
  features:
    - navigation.tabs
    - navigation.sections
    - navigation.expand
    - navigation.top
    - search.suggest
    - search.highlight
    - content.code.copy
    - content.code.annotate

plugins:
  - search
  - mermaid2

markdown_extensions:
  - pymdownx.highlight:
      anchor_linenums: true
  - pymdownx.inlinehilite
  - pymdownx.snippets
  - pymdownx.superfences:
      custom_fences:
        - name: mermaid
          class: mermaid
          format: !!python/name:pymdownx.superfences.fence_code_format
  - pymdownx.tabbed:
      alternate_style: true
  - admonition
  - pymdownx.details
  - pymdownx.emoji:
      emoji_index: !!python/name:material.extensions.emoji.twemoji
      emoji_generator: !!python/name:material.extensions.emoji.to_svg
  - attr_list
  - md_in_html
  - toc:
      permalink: true

docs.title: Step 3: Test Locally
docs.text:
Before deploying, test your documentation locally:

# Start local development server
mkdocs serve

# Open your browser to http://localhost:8000

Verify: - All pages load correctly - Navigation works - No broken links - Mermaid diagrams render properly

docs.title: Option A: Manual Deployment (Recommended for First Time)
docs.text:
# Build and deploy to GitHub Pages
mkdocs gh-deploy

# This will:
# 1. Build the documentation
# 2. Create/update the gh-pages branch
# 3. Push to GitHub

What happens: - MkDocs builds your site into static HTML - Creates a gh-pages branch (if it doesn't exist) - Pushes the built site to the gh-pages branch - GitHub Pages automatically serves from this branch

docs.title: Option B: Automated Deployment with GitHub Actions
docs.text:
Create .github/workflows/docs.yml:

name: Deploy Documentation

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
    paths:
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'mkdocs.yml'
      - '.github/workflows/docs.yml'

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        with:
          python-version: 3.x

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          pip install mkdocs mkdocs-material pymdown-extensions

      - name: Deploy documentation
        run: mkdocs gh-deploy --force

Commit and push: 

git add .github/workflows/docs.yml
git commit -m "Add automated documentation deployment"
git push

Now, every time you push changes to docs/ or mkdocs.yml, the documentation will automatically rebuild and deploy!

docs.text:
1. Go to your GitHub repository
  2. Click Settings → Pages
  3. Under Source, select:
  4. Branch: gh-pages
  5. Folder: / (root)
  6. Click Save

GitHub will show you the URL where your docs are published: 

https://yourusername.github.io/lixy/

docs.title: Step 6: Verify Deployment
docs.text:
1. Wait 1-2 minutes for GitHub Pages to build
  2. Visit your documentation URL
  3. Verify all pages work correctly

docs.title: Issue: "gh-pages branch not found"
docs.text:
Solution: 

# Create gh-pages branch manually
git checkout --orphan gh-pages
git reset --hard
git commit --allow-empty -m "Initialize gh-pages branch"
git push origin gh-pages
git checkout main

# Then run deployment again
mkdocs gh-deploy

docs.title: Issue: "Permission denied"
docs.text:
Solution: 

# Ensure you have write access to the repository
# Check your Git credentials
git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "your.email@example.com"

# For GitHub Actions, ensure the workflow has write permissions
# (Already configured in the workflow above)

docs.title: Issue: "404 Not Found" after deployment
docs.text: Solution: 1. Check GitHub Pages settings (Step 5) 2. Ensure gh-pages branch exists 3. Wait a few minutes for GitHub to process 4. Clear browser cache and try again

docs.title: Issue: Mermaid diagrams not rendering
docs.text:
Solution: 

# Install mermaid2 plugin
pip install mkdocs-mermaid2-plugin

# Ensure it's in mkdocs.yml plugins section

# 2. Test locally
mkdocs serve

# 3. Deploy
mkdocs gh-deploy

docs.title: Automatic Updates (with GitHub Actions)

git add docs/
git commit -m "Update documentation"
git push

To use a custom domain like docs.yoursite.com:

  1. Create a file docs/CNAME with your domain:

  3. Add a CNAME record pointing to yourusername.github.io

  • Deploy with mkdocs gh-deploy

docs.title: Authentication System Testing Guide
docs.text: This guide provides step-by-step instructions for testing the complete user authentication flow in Lixy.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Backend Dependencies: 

    cd cmd/lixy
go mod download

  2. Frontend Dependencies: 

    cd ../lixy-ui
npm install
# Install Pinia if not already installed
npm install pinia

  3. Environment Setup: Create or update .env file in cmd/lixy/: 

    JWT_SECRET=your-secret-key-change-this-in-production
CONTROLLER_PORT=8080

docs.title: 1. Start the Backend
docs.text:
cd cmd/lixy
go run main.go

Expected Output: 

INFO: Initializing default admin user...
INFO: Default admin user created successfully
INFO: Starting Lixy Controller on :8080

Verify: - Controller starts without errors - Default admin user is created - Database file created at cmd/lixy/lixy.db

docs.title: 2. Start the Frontend
docs.text:
In a new terminal: 

cd ../lixy-ui
npm run serve

Expected Output: 

App running at:
- Local:   http://localhost:8081/
- Network: http://192.168.x.x:8081/

Verify: - Frontend builds successfully - No compilation errors - Development server running

docs.title: 3. Test Initial Login
docs.text:
1. Navigate to: http://localhost:8081
  2. Expected: Redirected to /login page
  3. Login with default credentials:
  4. Username: admin
  5. Password: changeme
  6. Expected: Password change dialog appears

Verify: - Login form displays correctly - Form validation works (try empty fields) - Error messages display for invalid credentials

docs.title: 4. Test Password Change
docs.text:
1. In the password change dialog:
  2. Current Password: changeme
  3. New Password: Admin123! (or your choice, min 8 chars)
  4. Confirm Password: Admin123!
  5. Click "Change Password"
  6. Expected: Redirected to dashboard

Verify: - Password validation works (min 8 characters) - Passwords must match - Success redirects to dashboard - Navigation drawer appears with user info

docs.title: 5. Test Dashboard Access
docs.text:
Expected: - Dashboard loads successfully - Navigation drawer shows: - User info (admin / admin role) - All menu items - "User Management" link (admin only) - Logout button - Connection status shows "Online"

Verify: - All navigation links work - User avatar and info display correctly - Admin-only menu items visible

docs.title: 6. Test User Management (Admin)
docs.text:
1. Click "User Management" in sidebar
  2. Expected: User management page loads
  3. Click "Create User"
  4. Fill in form:
  5. Username: testuser
  6. Password: TestPass123!
  7. Role: user
  8. Check "Require password change on first login"
  9. Click "Create"
  10. Expected: User appears in table

Verify: - User creation form validates correctly - New user appears in list - User details display correctly (role, must_change_password flag)

docs.title: 7. Test User CRUD Operations
docs.text:
Edit User: 1. Click pencil icon on testuser 2. Change role to admin 3. Click "Update" 4. Verify: Role updated in table

Reset Password: 1. Click lock icon on testuser 2. Enter new password: NewPass123! 3. Check "Require password change on next login" 4. Click "Reset Password" 5. Verify: Success message, warning icon appears

Delete User: 1. Click delete icon on testuser 2. Confirm deletion 3. Verify: User removed from table

docs.title: 8. Test Logout
docs.text:
1. Click "Logout" in navigation drawer
  2. Expected: Redirected to /login
  3. Try accessing dashboard: http://localhost:8081/
  4. Expected: Redirected back to /login

Verify: - Logout clears token from localStorage - Protected routes redirect to login - Navigation drawer hidden on login page

docs.title: 9. Test Login with New Password
docs.text:
1. Login again:
  2. Username: admin
  3. Password: Admin123! (your new password)
  4. Expected: Direct access to dashboard (no password change required)

Verify: - Login successful with new password - No password change dialog - Dashboard loads immediately

docs.title: 10. Test Non-Admin User
docs.text:
1. Create a regular user (as admin):
  2. Username: regularuser
  3. Password: Regular123!
  4. Role: user
  5. Don't require password change
  6. Logout
  7. Login as regularuser
  8. Expected: Dashboard loads, but no "User Management" link

Verify: - Regular users cannot see admin menu items - Attempting to access /users redirects to dashboard - All other features work normally

docs.title: 11. Test Token Expiration
docs.text:
Manual Test: 1. Login as admin 2. Open browser DevTools → Application → Local Storage 3. Find lixy_token and note the expiry time 4. Modify the token to an expired one or wait for expiration 5. Navigate to any page 6. Expected: Automatic redirect to login

Verify: - Expired tokens trigger logout - User redirected to login page - Error message displayed (optional)

docs.title: 12. Test API Authentication
docs.text:
Using curl:

# Login and get token
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/auth/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"username":"admin","password":"Admin123!"}' \
  | jq -r '.token')

# Use token to access protected endpoint
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This document summarizes the implementation of GitHub App server-to-server authentication for Lixy. The GitHub App service is available for GitHub API operations but NOT used for container registry authentication due to GitHub limitations.

docs.title: Implementation Date
docs.text: November 2024

docs.title: Problem Statement
docs.text:
The original implementation required storing long-lived registry credentials or using OAuth flows that required user interaction. This was problematic for:

  • Automated deployments
  • CI/CD pipelines
  • Security (long-lived credentials)
  • Token rotation
  • Audit trails

docs.title: Initial Approach (Deprecated)
docs.text: Attempted to use GitHub App authentication for GHCR access, but discovered a critical limitation: - GitHub Apps cannot pull from GHCR - This is a known GitHub limitation that has existed for 5+ years - GitHub App tokens work for authentication but fail with "denied" errors when pulling packages

docs.title: Current Architecture
docs.text:
1. GitHub App Service - Available for GitHub API operations (webhooks, repository management, etc.)
  2. Registry Credential Store - Used for ALL registry authentication including GHCR
  3. Personal Access Tokens (PAT) - Recommended for GHCR authentication with read:packages scope
  4. Secure Storage - All credentials encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM
  5. Token Management - 15-minute scoped tokens issued to agents

docs.title: 1. GitHubAppService (internal/services/github_app_service.go)
docs.text:
Purpose: Manages GitHub App authentication and installation token generation

Key Features: - JWT generation using App ID and private key - Installation ID auto-discovery - Installation token request and caching - Token expiry management (1-hour tokens, 5-minute refresh buffer)

Key Methods: - GetInstallationToken() - Returns valid installation token (cached or new) - createGitHubAppJWT() - Generates JWT for GitHub API authentication - getInstallationID() - Discovers and caches installation ID - requestInstallationToken() - Requests new token from GitHub API - InvalidateCache() - Clears cached token - IsConfigured() - Checks if GitHub App is properly configured

Token Caching Strategy: 

// Cache token until 5 minutes before expiry
if cachedToken != nil && time.Now().Before(cachedToken.ExpiresAt.Add(-5*time.Minute)) {
    return cachedToken // Use cached token
}
// Otherwise, generate new token

docs.title: 2. Simplified PullTokenService (internal/services/pull_token_service.go)
docs.text:
Changes: - Removed GitHub App dependency for registry authentication - Simplified to always use registry credential store - All registries (including GHCR) use stored credentials

Flow: 

func (s *PullTokenService) GeneratePullToken(agentName, registry string) (*PullTokenResponse, error) {
    // All registries use stored credentials
    cred, err := s.credStore.GetCredential(registry)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get credentials for registry %s: %w", registry, err)
    }

    // Return credentials with audit logging
    return &PullTokenResponse{
        Token:     cred.Token,
        Username:  cred.Username,
        Registry:  registry,
        ExpiresIn: int(s.tokenTTL.Seconds()),
        ExpiresAt: time.Now().Add(s.tokenTTL),
    }, nil
}

docs.title: 3. Updated Factory (internal/client/factory.go)
docs.text:
Changes: - Initialize GitHubAppService (kept for potential GitHub API operations) - PullTokenService no longer depends on GitHubAppService

// Initialize GitHub App service (kept for potential GitHub API operations)
// Note: Registry authentication now uses stored credentials exclusively
_ = services.NewGitHubAppService(logger, configStore)

// Initialize pull token service with registry credential store
pullTokenService := services.NewPullTokenService(logger, registryCredStore, jwtSecret)

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              Registry Credential Authentication Flow             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

1. Agent Requests Pull Token
   ┌─────────┐
   │  Agent  │ ──── POST /api/pull-token ───>
   └─────────┘      { registry: "ghcr.io" }

2. Controller Retrieves Stored Credentials
   ┌────────────┐
   │ Controller │ ──── Get Credentials ───> RegistryCredentialStore
   └────────────┘                           (encrypted in database)

                           <─── { username: "user", token: "ghp_xxx" }

3. Generate Audit Token (15-minute validity)
   ┌────────────────────┐
   │ PullTokenService   │ ──── Create JWT for audit trail
   └────────────────────┘      Claims: { agent, registry, exp: now+15m }

4. Return to Agent
   ┌────────────┐
   │ Controller │ ──── { token: "ghp_xxx", username: "user" } ───> Agent
   └────────────┘

5. Agent Caches Token (15 minutes)
   ┌─────────┐
   │  Agent  │ ──── Store in memory cache
   └─────────┘      (reuse until expiry)

6. Agent Authenticates with Registry
   ┌─────────┐
   │  Agent  │ ──── docker login ghcr.io -u user -p ghp_xxx
   └─────────┘

                    ──── docker pull ghcr.io/org/image:latest ───> GHCR

docs.title: GitHub App Setup Guide
docs.text: This guide explains how to set up GitHub App authentication for Lixy to access GitHub Container Registry (GHCR) without user interaction.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Lixy uses GitHub App server-to-server authentication to generate installation access tokens for pulling private container images from GHCR. This approach:

  • ✅ No user interaction required - fully automated
  • ✅ Short-lived tokens - 1 hour maximum, auto-refreshed
  • ✅ Secure - private keys never leave the controller
  • ✅ Fine-grained permissions - only what's needed
  • ✅ Audit trail - all actions logged by GitHub

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• GitHub organization or personal account
  • Admin access to create GitHub Apps
  • Lixy controller running

docs.title: 1.1 Navigate to GitHub App Settings
docs.text:
For Organization: 

https://github.com/organizations/YOUR_ORG/settings/apps/new

For Personal Account: 

https://github.com/settings/apps/new

docs.title: 1.2 Configure GitHub App
docs.text:
Fill in the following fields:

GitHub App name: lixy-registry-access (or your preferred name)

Homepage URL: https://your-lixy-controller.example.com (or http://localhost:8080 for testing)

Webhook: - ☐ Uncheck "Active" (we don't need webhooks)

Permissions:

Repository permissions: - Contents: Read-only (to access container images) - Metadata: Read-only (required, automatically selected)

Where can this GitHub App be installed? - ☑ Only on this account

docs.title: 1.3 Create the App
docs.text: Click "Create GitHub App"

docs.title: 1.4 Generate Private Key
docs.text:
After creating the app:

  1. Scroll down to "Private keys" section
  2. Click "Generate a private key"
  3. A .pem file will be downloaded automatically
  4. Save this file securely - you'll need it for configuration

docs.title: 1.5 Note the App ID
docs.text:
At the top of the page, you'll see: 

App ID: 123456

Save this number - you'll need it for configuration.

docs.title: 2.1 Install on Your Account/Organization
docs.text:
1. Click "Install App" in the left sidebar
  2. Select your organization or personal account
  3. Choose installation scope:
  4. All repositories (recommended for simplicity)
  5. Only select repositories (if you want to limit access)
  6. Click "Install"

docs.title: 2.2 Note Installation ID (Optional)
docs.text:
The installation ID will be auto-discovered by Lixy, but you can find it in the URL: 

https://github.com/settings/installations/12345678
                                            ^^^^^^^^
                                         Installation ID

docs.title: 3.1 Prepare Private Key
docs.text:
Open the downloaded .pem file and copy its contents:

cat ~/Downloads/lixy-registry-access.2024-01-15.private-key.pem

You'll see something like: 

-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----
MIIEpAIBAAKCAQEA...
...
-----END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----

docs.title: 3.2 Configure via API
docs.text:
Use the Lixy API to store the GitHub App credentials:

curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/github/config \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_CONTROLLER_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "123456",
    "private_key": "-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----\nMIIEpAIBAAKCAQEA...\n-----END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----"
  }'

Important: Replace: - YOUR_CONTROLLER_TOKEN with your actual controller authentication token - 123456 with your actual App ID - The private_key value with your actual private key (keep the \n for newlines)

docs.title: 3.3 Verify Configuration
docs.text:
Check that the configuration was saved:

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_CONTROLLER_TOKEN" \
     http://localhost:8080/api/github/config

Expected response: 

{
  "client_id_configured": true,
  "private_key_configured": true,
  "redirect_uri": "http://localhost:8080/github/callback",
  "auth_url": "/github/auth",
  "callback_url": "/github/callback"
}

docs.title: 4.1 Request a Pull Token
docs.text:
From an agent, request a pull token for GHCR:

# This happens automatically when deploying, but you can test manually:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/pull-token \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer AGENT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "agent_name": "test-agent",
    "registry": "ghcr"
  }'

Expected response: 

{
  "token": "ghs_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",
  "username": "123456",
  "registry": "ghcr.io",
  "expires_in": 3600,
  "expires_at": "2024-01-15T12:00:00Z"
}

Note: The username field contains your GitHub App ID.

docs.title: 4.2 Test Docker Login
docs.text:
Use the token to authenticate with GHCR (username is your App ID):

echo "ghs_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx" | docker login ghcr.io -u 123456 --password-stdin

Replace 123456 with your actual GitHub App ID.

Expected output: 

Login Succeeded

  11. Automatically refreshes when needed

  12. Agent Usage

  13. Agent receives installation token
  14. Uses token to authenticate with GHCR
  15. Token works for all repositories the app is installed on

docs.title: GitHub App (Server-to-Server) ✅ Recommended for GHCR
docs.text:
Use for: Container registry access, automated deployments

Advantages: - ✅ No user interaction required - fully automated - ✅ Uses App ID + Private Key (PEM) - ✅ More secure and flexible - ✅ Short-lived tokens (1 hour, auto-refreshed) - ✅ Can act on behalf of the app - ✅ Better permissions model - ✅ Fine-grained repository access

Authentication Flow: 1. Configure App ID + Private Key via /api/github/config 2. Controller generates JWT using private key 3. Controller requests installation access token from GitHub API 4. Token used to authenticate with GHCR (ghcr.io) 5. Tokens automatically refreshed every hour

Setup: See GitHub App Setup Guide

docs.title: OAuth App (User Authentication) ⚠️ Requires User Interaction
docs.text:
Use for: User login, personal access

Characteristics: - ⚠️ Requires user interaction - user must click "Authorize" - Uses Client ID + Client Secret - Simpler but less flexible - Only user-level permissions - Requires OAuth callback flow

Authentication Flow: 1. Configure app credentials via /api/github/config 2. Start OAuth flow: Redirect user to /github/auth 3. User clicks "Authorize" on GitHub 4. Handle callback: GitHub redirects to /github/callback 5. Exchange code for access token 6. User authenticated with GitHub

docs.title: Security Features
docs.text:
• AES-GCM Encryption: Private keys encrypted at rest
  • PEM Key Storage: Secure storage of RSA private keys
  • JWT Signing: Proper GitHub App authentication
  • No plaintext storage: Keys never stored in plaintext

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Repository Setup: Add GitOps repository via API
  2. Auto-Sync: Controller periodically pulls latest changes from Git
  3. Tag Fetching: Controller fetches available image tags from container registries (GitHub Container Registry, Docker Hub)
  4. Version Filtering: Apply version strategies to filter allowed tags
  5. Reconciliation: Parse templates, render with variables, create/update deployments in database
  6. Agent Deployment: Agents poll controller, pull docker-compose files and deploy (agents handle image pulling)
  7. State Tracking: Record deployed state in state/ directory with deployment hashes
  8. Drift Detection: Compare desired vs actual state, auto-remediate if enabled
  9. Update Detection: Check for newer image versions based on version strategies

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Template-based: Reusable Go templates with variables
  • Multi-environment: Separate configs for dev/staging/production
  • Version Strategies: Control how versions are updated
  • Tag Fetching: Fetch available tags from GitHub Container Registry and Docker Hub
  • State Management: Track what's deployed where with deployment hashes
  • Drift Detection: Automatic detection and remediation
  • Update Detection: Check for newer versions based on strategies
  • Separation of Concerns: Controller manages state, agents handle deployment
  • No Docker on Controller: Controller only fetches metadata, doesn't pull images
  • Dependency Management: Handle service dependencies

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This document describes the architecture for secure registry credential management in Lixy, implementing a token-based authentication system where:

  • Controller stores and manages GHCR credentials securely
  • Agents request temporary pull tokens from the controller when needed
  • Controller issues scoped, time-limited tokens for specific agents
  • Agents use these tokens to authenticate with GHCR during image pulls

docs.title: Design Decisions
docs.text:
Based on requirements analysis:

  • Registry Focus: GitHub Container Registry (GHCR) only
  • Token Scope: Per-agent (token valid for all images an agent needs to pull)
  • Token Lifetime: 15 minutes (900 seconds)
  • Token Request: On-demand only (agents request tokens when needed for pull operations)
  • Credential Management: CLI commands and API endpoints

docs.title: 3. Data Flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Admin
    participant Controller
    participant CredStore
    participant Agent
    participant GHCR

    Note over Admin,Controller: 1. Initial Setup
    Admin->>Controller: Store GHCR credentials (CLI/API)
    Controller->>CredStore: Encrypt and store credentials
    CredStore-->>Controller: Credentials stored

    Note over Agent,GHCR: 2. Deployment Time
    Agent->>Agent: Deployment requires image pull
    Agent->>Controller: Request pull token (authenticated)
    Controller->>Controller: Validate agent authentication
    Controller->>CredStore: Retrieve GHCR credentials
    CredStore-->>Controller: Decrypted credentials
    Controller->>Controller: Generate 15-min JWT token
    Controller-->>Agent: Return token + username

    Agent->>Agent: docker login ghcr.io
    Agent->>GHCR: Pull image with credentials
    GHCR-->>Agent: Image layers
    Agent->>Agent: docker logout ghcr.io
    Agent->>Agent: Deploy container

docs.title: 4.1 Credential Storage
docs.text:
• Encryption: GHCR tokens encrypted using AES-256-GCM (existing ConfigStore encryption)
  • Key Management: Encryption key from LIXY_ENCRYPTION_KEY environment variable
  • Access Control: Only controller has access to encrypted credentials
  • Rotation: Support for credential rotation without agent reconfiguration

docs.title: 4.2 Pull Token Security
docs.text:
• Short-lived: 15-minute expiration reduces exposure window
  • Scoped: Tokens scoped to specific agent (via agent name in JWT)
  • One-time use: Tokens should be used immediately and not stored long-term
  • Audit Trail: All token issuance logged with agent name and timestamp

docs.title: 4.3 Transport Security
docs.text:
• TLS Required: All controller-agent communication over HTTPS
  • Agent Authentication: Agents must authenticate with permanent token before requesting pull token
  • Token Transmission: Pull tokens transmitted in HTTPS response body (not in URLs)

docs.title: 4.4 Token Validation
docs.text:
• JWT Signature: Tokens signed with controller's JWT secret
  • Expiration Check: Strict expiration validation
  • Agent Verification: Token agent_name must match requesting agent
  • Registry Validation: Token registry must match requested registry

docs.title: Conclusion

This architecture provides a secure, scalable foundation for registry credential management in Lixy. The design prioritizes security through encryption, short-lived tokens, and proper scoping while maintaining operational simplicity with on-demand token requests and straightforward CLI management.

The implementation follows the principle of least privilege: agents never have direct access to long-lived registry credentials, only temporary pull tokens scoped to their specific needs.

package services

import (
    "fmt"
    "time"
    "log/slog"
    "github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5"
    "github.com/MinaroShikuchi/lixy/internal/store"
)

// PullTokenClaims represents JWT claims for pull tokens
type PullTokenClaims struct {
    AgentName string `json:"agent_name"`
    Registry  string `json:"registry"`
    jwt.RegisteredClaims
}

// PullTokenResponse represents the response when issuing a pull token
type PullTokenResponse struct {
    Token     string    `json:"token"`
    Username  string    `json:"username"`
    Registry  string    `json:"registry"`
    ExpiresIn int       `json:"expires_in"`
    ExpiresAt time.Time `json:"expires_at"`
}

// PullTokenService manages pull token generation and validation
type PullTokenService struct {
    logger      *slog.Logger
    credStore   *store.RegistryCredentialStore
    jwtSecret   []byte
    tokenTTL    time.Duration // 15 minutes
}

// NewPullTokenService creates a new pull token service
func NewPullTokenService(
    logger *slog.Logger,
    credStore *store.RegistryCredentialStore,
    jwtSecret []byte,
) *PullTokenService

// GeneratePullToken generates a temporary pull token for an agent
func (s *PullTokenService) GeneratePullToken(agentName, registry string) (*PullTokenResponse, error)

// ValidatePullToken validates a pull token and returns its claims
func (s *PullTokenService) ValidatePullToken(tokenString string) (*PullTokenClaims, error)

// GetRegistryCredentials retrieves credentials for a registry
func (s *PullTokenService) GetRegistryCredentials(registry string) (*store.RegistryCredential, error)

Token Generation Logic: 

func (s *PullTokenService) GeneratePullToken(agentName, registry string) (*PullTokenResponse, error) {
    // 1. Retrieve registry credentials from store
    cred, err := s.credStore.GetCredential(registry)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get credentials: %w", err)
    }

    // 2. Create JWT claims
    expiresAt := time.Now().Add(s.tokenTTL)
    claims := &PullTokenClaims{
        AgentName: agentName,
        Registry:  registry,
        RegisteredClaims: jwt.RegisteredClaims{
            Subject:   "pull-token",
            ExpiresAt: jwt.NewNumericDate(expiresAt),
            IssuedAt:  jwt.NewNumericDate(time.Now()),
            ID:        generateTokenID(),
        },
    }

    // 3. Sign token
    token := jwt.NewWithClaims(jwt.SigningMethodHS256, claims)
    signedToken, err := token.SignedString(s.jwtSecret)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to sign token: %w", err)
    }

    // 4. Return response with actual registry token
    return &PullTokenResponse{
        Token:     cred.Token, // Return the actual GHCR token
        Username:  cred.Username,
        Registry:  "ghcr.io",
        ExpiresIn: int(s.tokenTTL.Seconds()),
        ExpiresAt: expiresAt,
    }, nil
}

    if r.Method != http.MethodPost {
        http.Error(w, "Method not allowed", http.StatusMethodNotAllowed)
        return
    }

    // 1. Extract agent name from context (set by auth middleware)
    agentName, ok := r.Context().Value(domain.AgentNameKey).(string)
    if !ok || agentName == "" {
        http.Error(w, "Agent not authenticated", http.StatusUnauthorized)
        return
    }

    // 2. Parse request
    var req PullTokenRequest
    if err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req); err != nil {
        http.Error(w, "Invalid request format", http.StatusBadRequest)
        return
    }

    // 3. Validate registry type
    if req.Registry != "ghcr" {
        http.Error(w, "Unsupported registry type", http.StatusBadRequest)
        return
    }

    // 4. Generate pull token
    tokenResp, err := h.pullTokenService.GeneratePullToken(agentName, req.Registry)
    if err != nil {
        h.logger.Error("Failed to generate pull token",
            "agent", agentName,
            "registry", req.Registry,
            "error", err)
        http.Error(w, "Failed to generate pull token", http.StatusInternalServerError)
        return
    }

    // 5. Log token issuance
    h.logger.Info("Pull token issued",
        "agent", agentName,
        "registry", req.Registry,
        "expires_at", tokenResp.ExpiresAt)

    // 6. Return response
    w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
    json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(PullTokenAPIResponse{
        Success:   true,
        Token:     tokenResp.Token,
        Username:  tokenResp.Username,
        Registry:  tokenResp.Registry,
        ExpiresIn: tokenResp.ExpiresIn,
        ExpiresAt: tokenResp.ExpiresAt.Format(time.RFC3339),
    })
}

package client

import (
    "bytes"
    "encoding/json"

    "time"

// PullTokenClient manages pull token requests and caching
type PullTokenClient struct {
    logger        *slog.Logger
    controllerURL string
    agentToken    string
    client        *http.Client
    tokenCache    map[string]*CachedToken
    cacheMutex    sync.RWMutex
}

// CachedToken represents a cached pull token
type CachedToken struct {
    Token     string
    Username  string
    Registry  string
    ExpiresAt time.Time
}

// PullTokenResponse matches controller response
type PullTokenResponse struct {
    Success   bool   `json:"success"`
    Token     string `json:"token"`
    Username  string `json:"username"`
    Registry  string `json:"registry"`
    ExpiresIn int    `json:"expires_in"`
    ExpiresAt string `json:"expires_at"`
    Error     string `json:"error,omitempty"`
}

// NewPullTokenClient creates a new pull token client
func NewPullTokenClient(
    logger *slog.Logger,
    controllerURL string,
    agentToken string,
) *PullTokenClient

// RequestPullToken requests a new pull token from the controller
func (c *PullTokenClient) RequestPullToken(registry string) (*CachedToken, error)

// GetCachedToken retrieves a cached token if still valid
func (c *PullTokenClient) GetCachedToken(registry string) (*CachedToken, bool)

// ClearExpiredTokens removes expired tokens from cache
func (c *PullTokenClient) ClearExpiredTokens()

// GetOrRequestToken gets cached token or requests new one
func (c *PullTokenClient) GetOrRequestToken(registry string) (*CachedToken, error)

Implementation: 

func (c *PullTokenClient) RequestPullToken(registry string) (*CachedToken, error) {
    // 1. Prepare request
    reqBody := map[string]string{"registry": registry}
    jsonData, err := json.Marshal(reqBody)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal request: %w", err)
    }

    // 2. Create HTTP request
    url := fmt.Sprintf("%s/api/pull-token", c.controllerURL)
    req, err := http.NewRequest("POST", url, bytes.NewBuffer(jsonData))
    if err != nil {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create request: %w", err)
    }

    // 3. Add authentication
    req.Header.Set("Authorization", fmt.Sprintf("Bearer %s", c.agentToken))
    req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")

    // 4. Send request
    resp, err := c.client.Do(req)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to send request: %w", err)
    }
    defer resp.Body.Close()

    // 5. Parse response
    var pullTokenResp PullTokenResponse
    if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&pullTokenResp); err != nil {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to decode response: %w", err)
    }

    if !pullTokenResp.Success {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("pull token request failed: %s", pullTokenResp.Error)
    }

    // 6. Parse expiration time
    expiresAt, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, pullTokenResp.ExpiresAt)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse expiration time: %w", err)
    }

    // 7. Cache token
    cached := &CachedToken{
        Token:     pullTokenResp.Token,
        Username:  pullTokenResp.Username,
        Registry:  pullTokenResp.Registry,
        ExpiresAt: expiresAt,
    }

    c.cacheMutex.Lock()
    c.tokenCache[registry] = cached
    c.cacheMutex.Unlock()

    c.logger.Info("Pull token received and cached",
        "registry", registry,
        "expires_at", expiresAt)

    return cached, nil
}

func (c *PullTokenClient) GetOrRequestToken(registry string) (*CachedToken, error) {
    // Check cache first
    if cached, ok := c.GetCachedToken(registry); ok {
        // Check if token expires in less than 1 minute
        if time.Until(cached.ExpiresAt) > time.Minute {
            c.logger.Debug("Using cached pull token", "registry", registry)
            return cached, nil
        }
    }

    // Request new token
    return c.RequestPullToken(registry)
}

func (cr *ContainerRuntime) AuthenticateRegistry(registry, username, token string) error {
    cmd := exec.Command(cr.Command, "login", registry, "-u", username, "--password-stdin")
    cmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader(token)

    output, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("registry authentication failed: %w, output: %s", err, string(output))
    }

    return nil
}

    cmd := exec.Command(cr.Command, "logout", registry)

    output, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("registry logout failed: %w, output: %s", err, string(output))
    }

    return nil
}

// PullImageWithAuth pulls an image with authentication
func (cr *ContainerRuntime) PullImageWithAuth(image, registry, username, token string) error {
    // 1. Authenticate
    if err := cr.AuthenticateRegistry(registry, username, token); err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("authentication failed: %w", err)
    }

    // 2. Pull image
    cmd := exec.Command(cr.Command, "pull", image)
    output, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()

    // 3. Logout (always, even on error)
    defer cr.LogoutRegistry(registry)

    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("image pull failed: %w, output: %s", err, string(output))
    }

    return nil
}

func (r *Reconciler) deployService(deployment *Deployment) error {

        if err != nil {

        }
    }

    // 4. Continue with deployment
    return r.deployWithCompose(deployment)
}

Agents automatically request pull tokens when deploying images from private registries. The process is:

  6. Logs out from registry

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
Q: How long do pull tokens last? A: 15 minutes. Agents cache tokens and automatically request new ones when expired.

Q: Can I use the same credentials for multiple agents? A: Yes, credentials are stored centrally in the controller and issued as scoped tokens to agents.

Q: What happens if credentials are deleted while agents are using them? A: Existing tokens continue to work until expiration. New token requests will fail.

Q: Can I rotate credentials without downtime? A: Yes, add new credentials before deleting old ones. Agents will use cached tokens until they expire.

Q: Are credentials backed up? A: Credentials are stored in the SQLite database. Back up both the database and encryption key.

Q: Can I export credentials? A: No, credentials are encrypted and cannot be exported in plaintext for security.

docs.title: Encryption at Rest
docs.text:
Credential Storage: - All registry credentials are encrypted using AES-256-GCM before storage - Encryption key must be provided via LIXY_ENCRYPTION_KEY environment variable - Key should be 32 bytes (256 bits) for AES-256 - Credentials are stored in SQLite database with encrypted token field

Key Management: 

# Generate a secure encryption key
openssl rand -base64 32

# Set the encryption key
export LIXY_ENCRYPTION_KEY="your-generated-key-here"

docs.title: Token Security
docs.text:
Pull Token Characteristics: - Type: JWT (JSON Web Tokens) - Expiration: 15 minutes (900 seconds) - Scope: Agent-specific via JWT claims - Signing: HMAC-SHA256 with secret key

JWT Claims: 

{
  "agent_name": "agent-hostname",
  "registry": "ghcr.io",
  "exp": 1699999999,
  "iat": 1699999099
}

docs.title: Transport Security
docs.text:
Controller-Agent Communication: - Pull token requests use HTTP POST to /api/pull-token - In production, should use HTTPS with TLS 1.2+ - Consider mutual TLS (mTLS) for agent authentication

CLI-Controller Communication: - Uses Unix domain socket (/tmp/lixy.sock) for local communication - Socket permissions should be restricted (0600)

docs.title: Problem Statement
docs.text: Currently, agents need to pull container images from private registries (like GHCR) but have no secure way to authenticate. Storing credentials directly on agents is a security risk.

docs.title: Solution

Implement a centralized credential management system where:

  1. Controller stores registry credentials securely (encrypted at rest)
  2. Agents request temporary pull tokens when needed
  3. Controller issues scoped, time-limited tokens (15 minutes)
  4. Agents use tokens to authenticate with registry during image pulls

docs.title: 2. Authentication Flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Browser
    participant LoginPage
    participant API
    participant UserService
    participant UserStore
    participant Database

    Browser->>LoginPage: Navigate to /login
    LoginPage->>Browser: Display login form

    Browser->>LoginPage: Enter credentials
    LoginPage->>API: POST /api/auth/login

    API->>UserService: Authenticate(username, password)
    UserService->>UserStore: GetUserByUsername(username)
    UserStore->>Database: SELECT * FROM users WHERE username=?
    Database-->>UserStore: User data
    UserStore-->>UserService: User object

    UserService->>UserService: Verify password hash

    alt Authentication Success
        UserService->>UserService: Generate JWT token
        UserService->>UserStore: UpdateLastLogin(userID)
        UserStore->>Database: UPDATE users SET last_login=?
        UserService-->>API: Token + User info
        API-->>LoginPage: {token, user, expiresIn}
        LoginPage->>Browser: Store token in localStorage
        LoginPage->>Browser: Redirect to dashboard
    else Authentication Failure
        UserService-->>API: Error: Invalid credentials
        API-->>LoginPage: 401 Unauthorized
        LoginPage->>Browser: Display error message
    end

func InitializeDefaultAdmin(userStore *UserStore) error {
    // Check if any admin users exist
    admins, err := userStore.GetUsersByRole("admin")
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }

    if len(admins) == 0 {
        // Create default admin
        defaultAdmin := User{
            Username: "admin",
            Password: "changeme",  // Will be hashed
            Role: "admin",
            MustChangePassword: true,
        }

        err := userStore.CreateUser(defaultAdmin)
        if err != nil {
            return err
        }

        log.Info("Default admin user created: admin/changeme")
        log.Warn("Please change the default password immediately")
    }

    return nil
}

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Lixy Controller now includes a complete user authentication system that replaces the manual token workflow. Users can log in through a web interface, and the system manages JWT tokens automatically.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Web-based Login: Modern login page with form validation
  • JWT Token Management: Automatic token storage and refresh
  • Default Admin User: Auto-initialized on first startup (username: admin, password: changeme)
  • Password Change Enforcement: Force password change on first login
  • User Management: Admin interface for creating and managing users
  • Role-Based Access Control: Admin and user roles with different permissions
  • Token Expiration Handling: Automatic logout when tokens expire
  • Dual Token Support: Separate authentication for web users and agents

docs.title: Password Security
docs.text:
• Bcrypt Hashing: All passwords hashed with bcrypt (cost factor: 12)
  • Minimum Length: 8 characters required
  • Force Password Change: Default admin must change password on first login
  • No Password Storage: Only hashes stored in database

docs.title: Token Security
docs.text:
• JWT Tokens: Signed with secret key from environment
  • 24-Hour Expiry: User tokens expire after 24 hours
  • Type Identification: Tokens include type field ("user" vs "authentication")
  • Automatic Expiry Monitoring: Frontend checks token expiry every minute
  • Secure Storage: Tokens stored in localStorage (HTTPS recommended)

docs.title: Access Control
docs.text:
• Role-Based Permissions: Admin vs user roles
  • Route Protection: Navigation guards enforce authentication
  • API Endpoint Protection: Middleware validates tokens and roles
  • Admin-Only Operations: User management restricted to admins

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text: This document provides a comprehensive overview of Lixy's architecture, components, and design decisions.

docs.title: System Architecture
docs.text:
Lixy follows a controller-agent architecture pattern, where a central controller manages the desired state and coordinates with distributed agents that execute deployments on LXC hosts.

graph TB
    subgraph "External Systems"
        GIT[Git Repository]
        REG[Container Registry]
        USER[Users/CLI]
    end

    subgraph "Controller"
        API[REST API]
        WEB[Web Dashboard]
        AUTH[Auth Service]
        GITOPS[GitOps Reconciler]
        DEPLOY[Deployment Service]
        AGENT_SVC[Agent Service]
        HEALTH[Health Service]
        DB[(SQLite DB)]
    end

    subgraph "Agent 1"
        A1_API[Agent API]
        A1_RUNTIME[Container Runtime]
        A1_LXC[LXC Containers]
    end

    subgraph "Agent 2"
        A2_API[Agent API]
        A2_RUNTIME[Container Runtime]
        A2_LXC[LXC Containers]
    end

    USER -->|HTTP/CLI| API
    USER -->|HTTPS| WEB
    GIT -->|Pull| GITOPS
    API --> AUTH
    API --> GITOPS
    API --> DEPLOY
    GITOPS --> DEPLOY
    DEPLOY --> AGENT_SVC
    AGENT_SVC -->|Commands| A1_API
    AGENT_SVC -->|Commands| A2_API
    A1_API --> A1_RUNTIME
    A2_API --> A2_RUNTIME
    A1_RUNTIME --> A1_LXC
    A2_RUNTIME --> A2_LXC
    A1_LXC -->|Pull Images| REG
    A2_LXC -->|Pull Images| REG
    HEALTH -->|Check| A1_API
    HEALTH -->|Check| A2_API
    AUTH --> DB
    DEPLOY --> DB
    AGENT_SVC --> DB

docs.title: Controller ↔ Agent
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Controller
    participant A as Agent

    Note over C,A: Agent Registration
    A->>C: Register (name, metadata)
    C->>A: Registration Token

    Note over C,A: Health Checking
    loop Every 30s
        C->>A: Health Check
        A->>C: Status (OK/Error)
    end

    Note over C,A: Deployment
    C->>A: Deploy Command (compose YAML)
    A->>A: Pull Images
    A->>A: Create Containers
    A->>C: Success/Failure

    Note over C,A: Updates
    C->>A: Update Command (new YAML)
    A->>A: Update Containers
    A->>C: Success/Failure

docs.title: GitOps Reconciliation
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant G as Git Repo
    participant C as Controller
    participant D as Database
    participant A as Agent

    Note over G,A: Reconciliation Cycle

    C->>G: Pull Latest Changes
    G->>C: Updated Files

    C->>C: Parse YAML Configs
    C->>D: Get Current State
    D->>C: Deployment List

    C->>C: Compare States

    alt New Deployment
        C->>D: Create Deployment
        C->>A: Deploy Command
        A->>C: Success
        C->>D: Update State
    else Updated Deployment
        C->>D: Update Deployment
        C->>A: Update Command
        A->>C: Success
        C->>D: Update State
    else Removed Deployment
        C->>A: Delete Command
        A->>C: Success
        C->>D: Delete Deployment
    end

docs.title: Authentication Flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant API as API Server
    participant Auth as Auth Service
    participant DB as Database

    U->>API: Login (username, password)
    API->>Auth: Validate Credentials
    Auth->>DB: Query User
    DB->>Auth: User Data
    Auth->>Auth: Verify Password (bcrypt)
    Auth->>Auth: Generate JWT
    Auth->>API: JWT Token
    API->>U: Token + User Info

    Note over U,DB: Subsequent Requests

    U->>API: Request + JWT
    API->>Auth: Validate JWT
    Auth->>API: User Context
    API->>API: Check Permissions
    API->>U: Response

// DeploymentService manages deployment lifecycle
type DeploymentService struct {

    store  *store.DeploymentStore
}

// CreateDeployment creates a new deployment
func (s *DeploymentService) CreateDeployment(name, target string, yaml []byte) error {
    // Validate inputs
    if name == "" {
        return fmt.Errorf("deployment name is required")
    }

    // Create deployment
    deployment := &store.Deployment{
        Name:        name,
        TargetLXC:   target,
        ComposeYAML: yaml,
    }

    return s.store.Create(deployment)
}

docs.text: This guide will walk you through installing and setting up Lixy on your system.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Before installing Lixy, ensure you have the following:

docs.title: Required
docs.text:
• Git - For GitOps workflows
  • LXC/LXD - On target hosts where containers will run
  • LXD 5.0 or higher recommended
  • Properly configured LXC networking

docs.title: Optional
docs.text: • Docker - For building and testing container images

docs.title: Controller Host
docs.text:
• OS: Linux (Ubuntu 20.04+, Debian 11+, or similar)
  • RAM: Minimum 512MB, recommended 1GB+
  • Disk: 1GB+ for application and data
  • Network: Accessible by all agents

docs.title: Agent Hosts
docs.text:

  • Disk: Sufficient for container images and data

docs.title: Download Pre-built Binaries
docs.text:
Download the latest release from GitHub Releases:

# Download and extract (example for Linux amd64)
wget https://github.com/MinaroShikuchi/lixy/releases/download/v1.0.0/lixy-linux-amd64.tar.gz
tar -xzf lixy-linux-amd64.tar.gz

# Install binaries
sudo mv lixy /usr/local/bin/
sudo mv lixies /usr/local/bin/

# Make them executable
sudo chmod +x /usr/local/bin/lixy
sudo chmod +x /usr/local/bin/lixies

# Verify installation
lixy version
lixies version

Available architectures: - lixy-linux-amd64.tar.gz - Linux 64-bit (Intel/AMD) - lixy-linux-arm64.tar.gz - Linux ARM 64-bit (Raspberry Pi, etc.) - lixy-darwin-amd64.tar.gz - macOS Intel - lixy-darwin-arm64.tar.gz - macOS Apple Silicon

Note: If you want to build from source for development purposes, see the Contributing Guide.

sudo lxd init

docs.text:
Run the initialization wizard:

sudo lxd init

Recommended settings: - Storage backend: dir or zfs - Network bridge: yes (creates lxdbr0) - IPv4 address: Auto - IPv6 address: Auto or none - LXD available over network: no (unless needed)

docs.text:

docs.title: 2. Create Configuration File
docs.text:
Create /etc/lixy/lixy.yaml:

# Controller configuration
server:
  host: "0.0.0.0"
  port: 8080

# Database configuration
database:
  path: "/var/lib/lixy/lixy.db"

# Git repository configuration
git:
  repos_path: "/var/lib/lixy/repos"
  poll_interval: "30s"

# Authentication
auth:
  jwt_secret: "change-this-to-a-secure-random-string"
  token_expiry: "24h"

# Logging
log:
  level: "info"
  format: "json"

docs.title: 3. Generate JWT Secret
docs.text:
# Generate a secure random string for JWT secret
openssl rand -base64 32

Update the jwt_secret in your configuration file with this value.

docs.title: 4. Set Permissions
docs.text:
sudo chown -R $USER:$USER /var/lib/lixy
sudo chmod 700 /etc/lixy
sudo chmod 600 /etc/lixy/lixy.yaml

docs.title: 5. Start the Controller
docs.text:
# Run in foreground
lixy

# Or run as a service (see systemd section below)

The controller will: - Start the HTTP server on port 8080 - Initialize the database - Create the default admin user (username: admin, password: admin) - Begin monitoring Git repositories

docs.title: 6. Verify Controller is Running
docs.text:
# Check health endpoint
curl http://localhost:8080/health

# Expected response:
# {"status":"healthy"}

docs.title: 1. Ensure LXD is Running
docs.text: sudo systemctl status snap.lxd.daemon

docs.title: 2. Get Registration Token
docs.text:
On the controller, generate a registration token:

lixy token create --type agent --name "my-agent"

This outputs a token like: agt_abc123...

docs.title: 3. Register the Agent
docs.text:
On the agent host:

lixies register \
  --controller http://controller-host:8080 \
  --token agt_abc123... \
  --name my-agent

The agent will: - Connect to the controller - Register itself - Start listening for deployment commands

docs.title: 4. Verify Agent Registration
docs.text:

lixy get agents

# Expected output:
# NAME       STATUS    LAST_SEEN

docs.title: Controller Service (systemd)

[Unit]
Description=Lixy Controller
After=network.target

Type=simple
User=lixy
Group=lixy
WorkingDirectory=/var/lib/lixy

docs.title: Getting Started with Lixy
docs.text: Welcome to Lixy! This guide will help you understand what Lixy is, how it works, and how to get started with your first deployment.

docs.title: What is Lixy?
docs.text:
Lixy is a GitOps deployment platform specifically designed for LXC containers. It brings modern DevOps practices to LXC container management by:

  • Storing infrastructure as code in Git repositories
  • Automatically reconciling desired state with actual state
  • Providing secure authentication for users and agents
  • Enabling drift detection and self-healing
  • Supporting multiple deployment strategies for version management

docs.title: Controller-Agent Architecture
docs.text:
Lixy uses a controller-agent architecture:

graph LR
    A[Controller] -->|Commands| B[Agent 1]
    A -->|Commands| C[Agent 2]
    A -->|Commands| D[Agent N]
    B -->|Status| A
    C -->|Status| A
    D -->|Status| A
    E[Git Repository] -->|Pull| A
    F[User/CLI] -->|API| A
  • Controller: Central management server that:
  • Monitors Git repositories for changes
  • Manages deployment state
  • Coordinates with agents

  • Provides API and web interface

  • Agents: Run on LXC hosts and:

  • Execute deployment commands
  • Report health status
  • Pull container images
  • Manage local containers

docs.title: GitOps Workflow
docs.text:
1. Declare your infrastructure in Git (YAML files)
  2. Commit changes to your repository
  3. Reconcile - Lixy detects changes and updates deployments
  4. Verify - Lixy ensures actual state matches desired state
  5. Heal - Lixy automatically fixes drift

docs.title: Deployments
docs.text: A deployment represents a containerized application defined by: - Docker Compose YAML configuration - Target agent (LXC host) - Environment variables - Version/tag information

docs.title: Environments
docs.text: Logical groupings of deployments (e.g., dev, staging, production) with: - Environment-specific variables - Shared configuration - Deployment strategies

docs.title: Strategies
docs.text: Rules for version updates: - Semver: Control major/minor/patch updates - Stability: Allow/block prereleases and RCs - Pattern: Regex-based version filtering - Fixed: Specific allowed versions only

docs.title: 1. Repository Structure
docs.text:
lixy-cd/
├── environments/
│   ├── dev/
│   │   ├── config.yaml          # Environment config
│   │   └── my-app.yaml          # Service definition
│   ├── staging/
│   └── production/
├── templates/
│   └── my-app/
│       └── docker-compose.yml.gotmpl
└── strategies/
    ├── dev-latest.yaml
    └── production-stable.yaml

docs.title: 2. Reconciliation Process
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Git
    participant Controller
    participant Agent
    participant LXC

    Git->>Controller: Webhook/Poll: Changes detected
    Controller->>Controller: Parse YAML configs
    Controller->>Controller: Compare desired vs actual
    Controller->>Agent: Deploy/Update command
    Agent->>LXC: Create/Update containers
    Agent->>Controller: Report status
    Controller->>Controller: Update state

docs.title: 3. Drift Detection
docs.text: Lixy continuously monitors for drift: - Compares deployment hashes - Detects missing deployments - Identifies unexpected changes - Automatically remediates (optional)

docs.title: Common Questions
docs.text:
Q: Can I deploy multiple services in one deployment? A: Yes! Use docker-compose with multiple services.

Q: How do I update to a new version? A: Use lixy update deployment <name> --compose <file> or update your GitOps repo.

Q: Can I use private registries? A: Yes! Add credentials with lixy create registry-credential.

Q: How do I backup my deployments? A: Your GitOps repository serves as the backup. For data, use LXC snapshots.

Q: Can I run Lixy in production? A: Yes! Follow security best practices and use HTTPS.

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text: Complete reference for the Lixy command-line interface.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Lixy provides two CLI tools: - lixy - Controller CLI for managing deployments, agents, and users - lixies - Agent CLI for registering and managing agents

docs.title: Global Flags
docs.text:
These flags are available for all commands:

--config string      Config file path (default: ./lixy.yaml)
--log-level string   Log level: debug, info, warn, error (default: info)
--log-format string  Log format: text, json (default: text)
--help, -h          Show help for command
--version, -v       Show version information

docs.title: lixy
docs.text:
Start the Lixy controller server.

lixy [flags]

Flags: - --host string - Server host (default: "0.0.0.0") - --port int - Server port (default: 8080) - --db-path string - Database file path (default: "./lixy.db")

Example: 

# Start with default settings
lixy

# Start on custom port
lixy --port 9090

# Start with custom database
lixy --db-path /var/lib/lixy/lixy.db

docs.title: lixy create deployment
docs.text:
Create a new deployment.

lixy create deployment NAME [flags]

Required Flags: - --target string - Target agent name - --compose string - Path to docker-compose.yml file

Optional Flags: - --yaml string - Inline YAML content (alternative to --compose) - --env-file string - Environment file path

Examples: 

# Create from file
lixy create deployment my-app \
  --target agent1 \
  --compose docker-compose.yml

# Create with inline YAML
lixy create deployment my-app \
  --target agent1 \
  --yaml 'version: "3"
services:
  web:
    image: nginx:latest'

# Create with environment file
lixy create deployment my-app \
  --target agent1 \
  --compose docker-compose.yml \
  --env-file .env

docs.title: lixy get deployments
docs.text:
List all deployments.

lixy get deployments [flags]

Flags: - --target string - Filter by target agent - --status string - Filter by status (running, stopped, failed) - --output string - Output format: table, json, yaml (default: table)

Examples: 

# List all deployments
lixy get deployments

# List deployments on specific agent
lixy get deployments --target agent1

# List running deployments
lixy get deployments --status running

# Output as JSON
lixy get deployments --output json

docs.title: lixy get deployment
docs.text:
Get details of a specific deployment.

lixy get deployment NAME [flags]

Flags: - --output string - Output format: table, json, yaml (default: table) - --verbose - Show detailed information

Examples: 

# Get deployment details
lixy get deployment my-app

# Get verbose output
lixy get deployment my-app --verbose

# Output as JSON
lixy get deployment my-app --output json

docs.title: lixy update deployment
docs.text:
Update an existing deployment.

lixy update deployment NAME [flags]

Flags: - --compose string - Path to new docker-compose.yml - --yaml string - Inline YAML content - --env-file string - Environment file path

Examples: 

# Update from file
lixy update deployment my-app --compose docker-compose.yml

# Update with inline YAML
lixy update deployment my-app --yaml 'version: "3"...'

docs.title: lixy delete deployment
docs.text:
Delete a deployment.

lixy delete deployment NAME [flags]

Flags: - --force - Skip confirmation prompt

Examples: 

# Delete with confirmation
lixy delete deployment my-app

# Force delete without confirmation
lixy delete deployment my-app --force

docs.title: lixy logs
docs.text:
View deployment logs.

lixy logs DEPLOYMENT [flags]

Flags: - --follow, -f - Follow log output - --tail int - Number of lines to show (default: all) - --since string - Show logs since timestamp (e.g., "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z") - --service string - Show logs for specific service

Examples: 

# View all logs
lixy logs my-app

# Follow logs in real-time
lixy logs my-app --follow

# Show last 100 lines
lixy logs my-app --tail 100

# Show logs since specific time
lixy logs my-app --since "2024-11-13T10:00:00Z"

# Show logs for specific service
lixy logs my-app --service web

docs.title: lixy get agents
docs.text:
List all registered agents.

lixy get agents [flags]

Flags: - --status string - Filter by status (online, offline) - --output string - Output format: table, json, yaml (default: table)

Examples: 

# List all agents
lixy get agents

# List online agents only
lixy get agents --status online

# Output as JSON
lixy get agents --output json

docs.title: lixy get agent
docs.text:
Get details of a specific agent.

lixy get agent NAME [flags]

Flags: - --output string - Output format: table, json, yaml (default: table)

Examples: 

# Get agent details
lixy get agent agent1

# Output as JSON
lixy get agent agent1 --output json

docs.title: lixy register-agent
docs.text:
Generate a registration token for a new agent.

lixy register-agent NAME [flags]

Flags: - --expires string - Token expiration duration (default: "24h")

Examples: 

# Generate token with default expiration
lixy register-agent agent1

# Generate token with custom expiration
lixy register-agent agent1 --expires 48h

docs.title: lixy delete agent
docs.text:
Unregister an agent.

lixy delete agent NAME [flags]

Flags: - --force - Skip confirmation prompt

Examples: 

# Delete with confirmation
lixy delete agent agent1

# Force delete
lixy delete agent agent1 --force

docs.title: lixy create user
docs.text:
Create a new user.

lixy create user USERNAME [flags]

Flags: - --password string - User password (prompted if not provided) - --role string - User role: admin, user (default: user)

Examples: 

# Create user with prompt for password
lixy create user developer

# Create user with password
lixy create user developer --password secret123

# Create admin user
lixy create user admin2 --role admin

docs.title: lixy get users
docs.text:
List all users.

lixy get users [flags]

Flags: - --role string - Filter by role (admin, user) - --output string - Output format: table, json, yaml (default: table)

Examples: 

# List all users
lixy get users

# List admin users only
lixy get users --role admin

# Output as JSON
lixy get users --output json

docs.title: lixy update user
docs.text:
Update user information.

lixy update user USERNAME [flags]

Flags: - --password - Change password (prompted) - --role string - Change role (admin, user)

Examples: 

# Change password
lixy update user developer --password

# Change role
lixy update user developer --role admin

# Change both
lixy update user developer --password --role admin

docs.title: lixy delete user
docs.text:
Delete a user.

lixy delete user USERNAME [flags]

Flags: - --force - Skip confirmation prompt

Examples: 

# Delete with confirmation
lixy delete user developer

# Force delete
lixy delete user developer --force

docs.title: lixy token create
docs.text:
Create an authentication token.

lixy token create [flags]

Flags: - --type string - Token type: agent, user (required) - --name string - Token name/identifier (required) - --expires string - Expiration duration (default: "24h")

Examples: 

# Create agent token
lixy token create --type agent --name agent1

# Create user token
lixy token create --type user --name developer

# Create token with custom expiration
lixy token create --type agent --name agent1 --expires 48h

docs.title: lixy token list
docs.text:
List all active tokens.

lixy token list [flags]

Flags: - --type string - Filter by type (agent, user) - --output string - Output format: table, json, yaml (default: table)

Examples: 

# List all tokens
lixy token list

# List agent tokens only
lixy token list --type agent

docs.title: lixy token revoke
docs.text:
Revoke a token.

lixy token revoke TOKEN [flags]

Examples: 

# Revoke a token

docs.title: lixy create registry-credential
docs.text:
Add registry credentials.

lixy create registry-credential NAME [flags]

Flags: - --url string - Registry URL (required) - --username string - Registry username (required) - --token string - Registry token/password (prompted if not provided)

Examples: 

# Create with prompt for token
lixy create registry-credential github \
  --url ghcr.io \
  --username myuser

# Create with token
lixy create registry-credential github \
  --url ghcr.io \
  --username myuser \
  --token ghp_abc123...

docs.title: lixy get registry-credentials
docs.text:
List registry credentials.

lixy get registry-credentials [flags]

Flags: - --output string - Output format: table, json, yaml (default: table)

Examples: 

# List all credentials
lixy get registry-credentials

# Output as JSON

docs.title: lixy delete registry-credential
docs.text:
Delete registry credentials.

lixy delete registry-credential NAME [flags]

Flags: - --force - Skip confirmation prompt

Examples: 

# Delete with confirmation
lixy delete registry-credential github

# Force delete
lixy delete registry-credential github --force

docs.title: lixy reconcile environment
docs.text:
Reconcile an environment from GitOps repository.

lixy reconcile environment NAME [flags]

Flags: - --repository string - Repository name (required) - --force - Force reconciliation even if no changes detected

Examples: 

# Reconcile dev environment
lixy reconcile environment dev --repository lixy-cd

# Force reconciliation
lixy reconcile environment dev --repository lixy-cd --force

docs.title: lixy create repository
docs.text:
Add a GitOps repository.

lixy create repository NAME [flags]

Flags: - --url string - Repository URL (required) - --branch string - Branch name (default: "main") - --token string - Access token for private repos - --poll-interval string - Polling interval (default: "30s")

Examples: 

# Add public repository
lixy create repository lixy-cd \
  --url https://github.com/user/lixy-cd.git

# Add private repository
lixy create repository lixy-cd \
  --url https://github.com/user/lixy-cd.git \
  --token ghp_abc123...

# Custom branch and poll interval
lixy create repository lixy-cd \
  --url https://github.com/user/lixy-cd.git \
  --branch develop \
  --poll-interval 60s

docs.title: lixy get repositories
docs.text:
List GitOps repositories.

lixy get repositories [flags]

Flags: - --output string - Output format: table, json, yaml (default: table)

Examples: 

# List all repositories
lixy get repositories

# Output as JSON
lixy get repositories --output json

docs.title: lixy delete repository
docs.text:

lixy delete repository NAME [flags]

Flags: - --force - Skip confirmation prompt

Examples: 

# Delete with confirmation
lixy delete repository lixy-cd

# Force delete
lixy delete repository lixy-cd --force

docs.title: lixy health

lixy health [flags]

docs.title: lixies register

lixies register \
  --controller http://controller:8080 \
  --token agt_abc123...

# Register with custom name

  --controller http://controller:8080 \
  --token agt_abc123... \
  --name my-agent

docs.title: lixies unregister

lixies unregister [flags]

docs.title: lixies check

docs.title: lixies

docs.title: Configuration Reference
docs.text: Complete reference for configuring Lixy controller and agents.

docs.title: Controller Configuration
docs.text: The controller can be configured using a YAML configuration file, environment variables, or command-line flags.

docs.title: Configuration File
docs.text:
Default location: ./lixy.yaml or /etc/lixy/lixy.yaml

# Server configuration
server:
  host: "0.0.0.0"              # Server bind address
  port: 8080                    # Server port
  read_timeout: "30s"           # HTTP read timeout
  write_timeout: "30s"          # HTTP write timeout
  shutdown_timeout: "10s"       # Graceful shutdown timeout

# Database configuration
database:
  path: "/var/lib/lixy/lixy.db" # SQLite database file path
  max_open_conns: 25            # Maximum open connections
  max_idle_conns: 5             # Maximum idle connections
  conn_max_lifetime: "1h"       # Connection maximum lifetime

# Git repository configuration
git:
  repos_path: "/var/lib/lixy/repos"  # Local repository storage path
  poll_interval: "30s"               # Repository polling interval
  clone_timeout: "5m"                # Git clone timeout
  pull_timeout: "2m"                 # Git pull timeout

# Authentication configuration
auth:
  jwt_secret: "change-this-secret"   # JWT signing secret (REQUIRED)
  token_expiry: "24h"                # Default token expiration
  agent_token_expiry: "720h"         # Agent token expiration (30 days)
  refresh_token_expiry: "168h"       # Refresh token expiration (7 days)

# Logging configuration
log:
  level: "info"                      # Log level: debug, info, warn, error
  format: "json"                     # Log format: json, text
  output: "stdout"                   # Log output: stdout, stderr, file path

# CORS configuration (for web dashboard)
cors:
  enabled: true                      # Enable CORS
  allowed_origins:                   # Allowed origins
    - "http://localhost:3000"
    - "http://localhost:8080"
  allowed_methods:                   # Allowed HTTP methods
    - "GET"
    - "POST"
    - "PUT"
    - "DELETE"
  allowed_headers:                   # Allowed headers
    - "Authorization"
    - "Content-Type"
  allow_credentials: true            # Allow credentials

# Rate limiting
rate_limit:
  enabled: true                      # Enable rate limiting
  requests_per_minute: 60            # Requests per minute per IP
  burst: 10                          # Burst size

# Drift detection
drift_detection:
  enabled: true                      # Enable drift detection
  check_interval: "5m"               # Check interval
  auto_heal: true                    # Automatically fix drift
  protected_services: []             # Services to exclude from auto-heal

# Metrics and monitoring
metrics:
  enabled: true                      # Enable Prometheus metrics
  path: "/metrics"                   # Metrics endpoint path

# TLS configuration (optional)
tls:
  enabled: false                     # Enable TLS
  cert_file: "/path/to/cert.pem"    # Certificate file
  key_file: "/path/to/key.pem"      # Private key file
  auto_cert: false                   # Use Let's Encrypt auto-cert
  auto_cert_domain: ""               # Domain for auto-cert

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
All configuration options can be set via environment variables using the LIXY_ prefix:

# Server
export LIXY_SERVER_HOST="0.0.0.0"
export LIXY_SERVER_PORT="8080"

# Database
export LIXY_DATABASE_PATH="/var/lib/lixy/lixy.db"

# Git
export LIXY_GIT_REPOS_PATH="/var/lib/lixy/repos"
export LIXY_GIT_POLL_INTERVAL="30s"

# Authentication
export LIXY_AUTH_JWT_SECRET="your-secret-key"
export LIXY_AUTH_TOKEN_EXPIRY="24h"

# Logging
export LIXY_LOG_LEVEL="info"
export LIXY_LOG_FORMAT="json"

docs.title: Command-Line Flags
docs.text:
lixy \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8080 \
  --db-path /var/lib/lixy/lixy.db \
  --log-level info \
  --log-format json

docs.title: Configuration Priority
docs.text:
Configuration is loaded in the following order (later sources override earlier ones):

  1. Default values
  2. Configuration file
  3. Environment variables
  4. Command-line flags

docs.title: Agent Configuration
docs.text: The agent can be configured using a YAML configuration file or environment variables.

docs.title: Configuration File
docs.text:
Default location: ./lixies.yaml or /etc/lixies/lixies.yaml

# Controller connection
controller:
  url: "http://controller:8080"      # Controller URL
  token: "agt_your_token_here"       # Agent authentication token
  timeout: "30s"                     # Request timeout
  retry_interval: "10s"              # Retry interval on connection failure
  max_retries: 5                     # Maximum retry attempts

# Agent configuration
agent:
  name: "my-agent"                   # Agent name (default: hostname)
  check_interval: "10s"              # Health check interval
  deployment_timeout: "5m"           # Deployment operation timeout
  cleanup_interval: "1h"             # Cleanup interval for old containers

# LXC configuration
lxc:
  socket_path: "/var/snap/lxd/common/lxd/unix.socket"  # LXD socket path
  timeout: "30s"                     # LXC operation timeout
  image_server: "https://images.linuxcontainers.org"   # Default image server

# Container runtime
runtime:
  pull_timeout: "10m"                # Image pull timeout
  start_timeout: "2m"                # Container start timeout
  stop_timeout: "30s"                # Container stop timeout
  remove_timeout: "1m"               # Container remove timeout

# Logging
log:
  level: "info"                      # Log level: debug, info, warn, error
  format: "json"                     # Log format: json, text
  output: "stdout"                   # Log output: stdout, stderr, file path

# Resource limits (optional)
limits:
  max_deployments: 50                # Maximum concurrent deployments
  max_cpu: "4"                       # Maximum CPU cores per deployment
  max_memory: "4GB"                  # Maximum memory per deployment
  max_disk: "20GB"                   # Maximum disk per deployment

# Networking (optional)
network:
  bridge: "lxdbr0"                   # Default network bridge
  ipv4_address: "auto"               # IPv4 address allocation
  ipv6_address: "none"               # IPv6 address allocation

docs.text:
Location: environments/<env-name>/config.yaml

name: dev                            # Environment name

# Environment variables

version: '3'
services:

    ports:
      - "{{ .PORT }}:80"
    environment:

      - API_URL={{ .API_URL }}
    {{- if .REPLICAS }}

    {{- end }}
    restart: unless-stopped
